moments.title: Early Homo sapiens
moments.description: Fossil evidence places early members of our species in Africa hundreds of thousands of years ago.

moments.title: Fire, Tools & Adaptation
moments.description: Controlled fire and increasingly specialized tools transformed food preparation, protection, and social life.

moments.title: Last Known Homo erectus
moments.description: New dating of fossils from Java indicates Homo erectus survived there until roughly 108,000–117,000 years ago.

moments.title: Settled Communities Expand
moments.description: In several regions, people increasingly combined hunting and gathering with more settled lifeways and food production.

moments.title: Lucy and Australopithecus afarensis
moments.description: The fossil skeleton known as Lucy became one of the most famous windows into early human evolution.

moments.title: Early Homo sapiens at Jebel Irhoud
moments.description: Fossils from Morocco pushed evidence for early Homo sapiens far deeper into Africa’s past.

moments.title: Symbolic Culture at Blombos Cave
moments.description: Engraved ochre, shell beads, and toolmaking evidence reveal complex symbolic behavior in southern Africa.

moments.title: Major Human Migrations Expand
moments.description: Homo sapiens populations spread into new regions, interacting with other human groups and adapting to varied environments.

moments.title: Last Glacial Maximum
moments.description: Ice sheets expanded, sea levels fell, and human communities adapted to colder and drier environments.

moments.title: Agriculture Takes Root
moments.description: Domestication of plants and animals developed independently in multiple regions and helped support larger settlements.

moments.title: Writing Systems Emerge
moments.description: Early writing systems developed to record transactions, institutions, stories, and political power.

moments.title: Pyramids of Giza
moments.description: Monumental building in Old Kingdom Egypt reflected centralized authority, religious beliefs, labor organization, and engineering.

moments.title: Hammurabi’s Judgments
moments.description: The famous Babylonian stela preserves a large collection of royal legal judgments and principles.

moments.title: Uruk and the Rise of Cities
moments.description: Large urban centers in Mesopotamia concentrated labor, administration, temples, trade, and political authority.

moments.title: Indus Valley Urban Civilization
moments.description: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro featured planned streets, drainage, craft production, and far-reaching trade.

moments.title: Kerma and Ancient Nubia
moments.description: Powerful Nubian states developed along the Nile south of Egypt, controlling trade routes and regional resources.

moments.title: Ironworking in Africa
moments.description: Iron production developed in parts of Africa and supported new tools, farming systems, crafts, and political growth.

moments.title: Hatshepsut
moments.description: One of ancient Egypt’s most successful female pharaohs used trade, monumental building, and royal imagery to strengthen her rule.

moments.title: Democracy in Athens
moments.description: Athenian political institutions expanded direct participation for male citizens while excluding many residents.

moments.title: Philosophies & Faith Traditions
moments.description: Influential traditions across South Asia, East Asia, the Mediterranean, and Southwest Asia shaped ethics and social life.

moments.title: Silk Roads Networks
moments.description: Overland and maritime routes linked merchants, states, travelers, technologies, religions, and disease across Eurasia.

moments.title: Kingdom of Kush at Meroë
moments.description: Kushite rulers governed a major Nile Valley state centered farther south at Meroë.

moments.title: Mauryan Empire and Ashoka
moments.description: A vast South Asian empire promoted imperial administration and, under Ashoka, inscriptions tied to Buddhist ethics.

moments.title: Imperial China Unifies
moments.description: Qin unification and the long Han era created durable institutions, infrastructure, and imperial traditions.

moments.title: Kingdom of Aksum
moments.description: Aksum became a Red Sea power linking the African interior, Arabia, the Mediterranean, and Indian Ocean trade.

moments.title: Classic Maya Cities
moments.description: Maya city-states developed monumental architecture, writing, astronomy, calendars, and complex political networks.

moments.title: Confucius
moments.description: A Chinese teacher and thinker whose ideas about ethics, education, family, and government shaped East Asian societies for centuries.

moments.title: Ashoka
moments.description: The Mauryan emperor promoted Buddhist ethics and public welfare after a brutal war of conquest.

moments.title: Hypatia of Alexandria
moments.description: A mathematician, astronomer, and philosopher who taught in one of the ancient Mediterranean’s great intellectual centers.

moments.title: Kingdoms & Courts
moments.description: Political authority took many forms, from kingdoms and empires to city-states and decentralized lordships.

moments.title: Centers of Learning Flourish
moments.description: Scholars across the Islamic world translated, preserved, debated, and extended knowledge in mathematics, medicine, astronomy, and philosophy.

moments.title: Crusading Movements
moments.description: A series of religiously framed military campaigns transformed politics, trade, and relations across the Mediterranean world.

moments.title: The Black Death
moments.description: Pandemic plague caused catastrophic mortality across Eurasia and North Africa and reshaped economies and communities.

moments.title: Ghana Empire and Trans-Saharan Trade
moments.description: West African states grew wealthy by controlling trade in gold, salt, and other goods across the Sahara.

moments.title: Swahili Coast City-States
moments.description: African port cities linked the East African coast to Arabia, Persia, India, and the wider Indian Ocean.

moments.title: Great Zimbabwe
moments.description: A major stone-built city became the center of a powerful southern African state tied to regional and Indian Ocean trade.

moments.title: Mali Empire
moments.description: Mali became one of medieval West Africa’s most influential states, controlling gold-producing regions and trade routes.

moments.title: Mansa Musa’s Pilgrimage
moments.description: The ruler of Mali traveled to Mecca with a famous caravan that advertised West Africa’s wealth and connections.

moments.title: The 1054 Supernova Remembered
moments.description: Centuries before the Black Death, skywatchers recorded a brilliant “guest star” later linked to the Crab Nebula.

moments.title: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
moments.description: A Persian polymath whose works on medicine and philosophy influenced scholarship from the Islamic world to Europe.

moments.title: Murasaki Shikibu
moments.description: A Japanese court writer associated with The Tale of Genji, often described as one of the world’s earliest great novels.

moments.title: Tenochtitlan Is Founded
moments.description: The Mexica established Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, laying the foundation for one of the largest cities in the Americas.

moments.title: Print Expands
moments.description: Movable-type printing in Europe accelerated the circulation of texts; printing traditions elsewhere had much earlier histories.

moments.title: Oceanic Networks Intensify
moments.description: European maritime expansion connected existing regional worlds through conquest, commerce, colonization, and forced migration.

moments.title: Scientific Revolution
moments.description: Observation, mathematics, instruments, and debate challenged inherited explanations of the natural world.

moments.title: Kingdom of Benin
moments.description: Benin developed a powerful court culture, urban center, regional trade, and extraordinary brass and ivory art.

moments.title: Kingdom of Kongo
moments.description: A Central African kingdom built regional power and later maintained diplomatic and religious connections with Portugal and the Atlantic world.

moments.title: Columbian Exchange
moments.description: Plants, animals, pathogens, and people moved between Afro-Eurasia and the Americas on an unprecedented scale.

moments.title: Atlantic Slave Trade Expands
moments.description: Millions of Africans were forcibly transported across the Atlantic in one of history’s largest coerced migrations.

moments.title: Songhai Falls, West African Networks Continue
moments.description: Moroccan forces defeated Songhai at Tondibi, but West African trade, scholarship, and political life continued through new states and networks.

moments.title: Queen Nzinga
moments.description: The ruler of Ndongo and Matamba used diplomacy, warfare, and shifting alliances to resist Portuguese expansion in Central Africa.

moments.title: Galileo Galilei
moments.description: Telescopic observation and mathematical analysis helped transform astronomy and debates about how knowledge should be tested.

moments.title: Gutenberg Bible Is Printed
moments.description: Movable metal type and the printing press helped accelerate the circulation of books in Europe.

moments.title: American Independence
moments.description: The Declaration of Independence articulated claims about rights and government while the Revolutionary War continued.

moments.title: Haitian Revolution
moments.description: Enslaved and free people in Saint-Domingue overthrew slavery and colonial rule, creating independent Haiti.

moments.title: Industrial Transformation
moments.description: Steam power, factories, railways, and mechanized production changed work, cities, consumption, and the environment.

moments.title: Abolition Expands
moments.description: Enslaved people, free Black activists, abolitionists, and political movements challenged slavery across the Atlantic world.

moments.title: American Revolutionary War
moments.description: Colonial rebellion against Britain became a war for independence with international dimensions.

moments.title: French Revolution
moments.description: Revolutionary upheaval dismantled old institutions, redefined citizenship, and reshaped European politics.

moments.title: Latin American Independence Movements
moments.description: Revolutions and wars ended Spanish and Portuguese colonial rule across much of the Americas.

moments.title: Mount Tambora Erupts
moments.description: A massive Indonesian eruption cooled global temperatures and contributed to the “Year Without a Summer.”

moments.title: First Opium War
moments.description: War between Britain and Qing China exposed the coercive power behind nineteenth-century imperial trade.

moments.title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
moments.description: A major uprising against East India Company rule transformed British governance in South Asia.

moments.title: American Civil War
moments.description: The United States fought a devastating civil war centered on slavery, secession, Union, and emancipation.

moments.title: Emancipation Proclamation
moments.description: Lincoln’s wartime proclamation declared enslaved people free in areas still in rebellion and authorized Black military service.

moments.title: Berlin Conference and the Scramble for Africa
moments.description: European powers formalized rules for imperial claims while excluding African representatives from the conference.

moments.title: Battle of Adwa
moments.description: Ethiopian forces defeated an invading Italian army and preserved Ethiopian sovereignty.

moments.title: Toussaint Louverture
moments.description: A formerly enslaved leader whose political and military leadership was central to the Haitian Revolution.

moments.title: Frederick Douglass
moments.description: After escaping slavery, Douglass became one of the nineteenth century’s most influential abolitionists, writers, and advocates for equal citizenship.

moments.title: Meiji Restoration
moments.description: Political change in Japan ended Tokugawa rule and began a rapid state-led transformation.

moments.title: First World War
moments.description: Industrialized warfare devastated Europe and other regions and accelerated political upheaval and imperial change.

moments.title: Great Depression
moments.description: A global economic crisis produced mass unemployment, political instability, and competing responses from governments.

moments.title: Second World War
moments.description: The deadliest war in history transformed states, societies, technologies, borders, and the international order.

moments.title: The Holocaust
moments.description: Nazi Germany and its collaborators persecuted and murdered six million Jews and millions of other victims.

moments.title: Cold War
moments.description: U.S.–Soviet rivalry shaped alliances, proxy wars, nuclear strategy, space exploration, and politics around the world.

moments.title: Armenian Genocide
moments.description: Ottoman authorities carried out mass deportations and killings of Armenians during World War I.

moments.title: Russian Revolution
moments.description: Revolution ended imperial rule and eventually brought the Bolsheviks to power.

moments.title: Ghana Gains Independence
moments.description: Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence from European rule in the postwar wave of decolonization.

moments.title: Year of Africa
moments.description: Seventeen African countries gained independence in 1960, dramatically reshaping the United Nations and world politics.

moments.title: March on Washington
moments.description: Hundreds of thousands gathered in Washington, D.C., demanding jobs, freedom, and civil rights.

moments.title: Soweto Uprising
moments.description: Black South African students protested apartheid education, and police violence triggered nationwide resistance.

moments.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
moments.description: Popular pressure and political change opened the Berlin Wall and accelerated the collapse of communist governments in Eastern Europe.

moments.title: Mahatma Gandhi
moments.description: Gandhi developed mass nonviolent resistance strategies that shaped India’s independence movement and influenced later civil-rights campaigns.

moments.title: Martin Luther King Jr.
moments.description: A Baptist minister and civil-rights leader who helped mobilize nonviolent campaigns against segregation and racial injustice in the United States.

moments.title: Harlem Renaissance
moments.description: Black writers, musicians, artists, and intellectuals transformed American culture and reshaped global ideas about Black identity and modernity.

moments.title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
moments.description: Humans landed on the Moon for the first time during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.

moments.title: The Web Goes Global
moments.description: Internet access and the World Wide Web increasingly transformed communication, commerce, education, and public life.

moments.title: September 11 Attacks
moments.description: Coordinated terrorist attacks in the United States killed nearly 3,000 people and profoundly affected U.S. and global policy.

moments.title: Mobile & Social Media Age
moments.description: Smartphones and social platforms altered news, relationships, organizing, entertainment, and public debate.

moments.title: South Africa’s First Multiracial Election
moments.description: Millions voted in the election that ended formal apartheid rule and brought Nelson Mandela to the presidency.

moments.title: Global Financial Crisis
moments.description: Failures in housing finance and interconnected credit markets triggered a severe global recession.

moments.title: Arab Spring
moments.description: Protest movements challenged governments across North Africa and the Middle East, producing very different outcomes.

moments.title: Paris Climate Agreement
moments.description: Nearly every nation adopted a framework to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions and strengthen climate adaptation.

moments.title: Brexit
moments.description: The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union and formally exited in 2020.

moments.title: COVID-19 Pandemic
moments.description: A novel coronavirus spread globally, causing mass illness and death and disrupting everyday life, economies, education, and politics.

moments.title: Wangari Maathai
moments.description: The Kenyan environmentalist and democracy advocate linked tree planting, women’s leadership, human rights, and sustainable development.

moments.title: Tim Berners-Lee and the World Wide Web
moments.description: A proposal at CERN evolved into the World Wide Web, transforming how people publish, link, and access information.

moments.title: Artificial Intelligence Becomes Everyday Infrastructure
moments.description: AI systems increasingly influence work, learning, medicine, logistics, creativity, research, and public policy.

moments.title: Generative AI Enters Mass Use
moments.description: Public-facing generative AI systems rapidly expanded the use of machine-generated text, images, audio, and code.

moments.title: Examine the Evidence
moments.description: History is not simply a list of dates. Ask what happened, what changed, whose perspectives survive, and what evidence supports a claim.
